cells.tense: You're tending it now — both hands on it, and it's holding.
cells.verb: keeping what you're growing in good shape, by hand, on purpose
cells.place: at the end of something you built and the start of what it opens into
cells.ask: Let someone who watched you tend this tell you what it took, and take the thanks without waving it off. When that lands, letting go reads as the reward instead of the loss.
cells.core: You're tending what you've grown, and it's holding. Two needs at once, held steady, neither one dropped — that's the work, and it worked. What you were growing has come up. Nothing here needs forcing anymore. Finished isn't over; it's the ground the next thing comes out of, and so are you.
cells.sheetLine: You brought it through. You get to hear that said out loud.

cells.tense: You're already tending next season before this one's in the barn.
cells.verb: keeping what you're growing in good shape, by hand, on purpose
cells.place: at the end of something you built and the start of what it opens into
cells.ask: Let one thing finish before the next one starts — complete it, hand it over, and let what comes back be satisfaction rather than a new list. Vision fed by finished ground is the vision that turns out true.
cells.core: You're managing a future that hasn't arrived. Every version of what's coming gets handled ahead of time — the thing not yet grown, the need not yet spoken, the ending you're bracing for — so your hands are always on the next field while this one stands ripe and untouched. The care is real. What it's aimed at isn't here yet, and none of the bracing makes the future safer. It only spends the one doing the tending.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a crop that hasn't been planted yet.

cells.tense: The tending sits behind you — the gate's still there, just on the other side now.
cells.verb: keeping what you're growing in good shape, by hand, on purpose
cells.place: at the end of something you built and the start of what it opens into
cells.ask: Pick one growing thing and hope for it out loud — say what you want it to become, to one person, this week. What you cultivated reaching its end is what makes the light; the hoping is how you turn back toward it.
cells.core: The care is still in you; it hasn't gone anywhere. The tending itself stopped — hands off, gate shut, that field standing back there untouched — and you're still standing at a door that's already behind you. What's quiet isn't the ability to tend. It's the reach, the hand going back out toward something that might grow.
cells.sheetLine: You have it in you to tend something. The hand's just not reaching.

cells.tense: Your hands are still on it — you just call it something else.
cells.verb: keeping what you're growing in good shape, by hand, on purpose
cells.place: at the end of something you built and the start of what it opens into
cells.ask: Say out loud that one of these things is yours — that you tended it, that you carried it — and let one person hear you say it. On the record, release stops feeling like surrender and starts feeling like the point.
cells.core: You're already the one tending it. You show up, you hold the thing steady, you carry two needs without dropping either — and you talk as if it happened on its own, as if you were only keeping the lights on. The care is running; the claim on it isn't. Whoever's been getting the credit for this, it hasn't been the person whose hands are on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already keeping this alive. You just haven't said so.
